Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (Model fit / evals)

Hi Samir —

Great to meet you and Elena today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goals: evaluate model options for Finvia's customer support summarization + intent extraction flows (1-2k tokens typical, 50k monthly active requests).
- Key constraints: p95 latency target <= 300ms, p99 < 700ms for sync endpoints; strict PII retention rules; prefer hosted but open to Dedicated if cost-effective.
- Action items we agreed on:
  1) Redwood to share model fit recommendations, benchmark links, and the prompt set we used for initial internal evals.
  2) Finvia to confirm any additional evaluation prompts and share sample redaction/PII policies.
  3) Schedule a sandbox run (we suggested slot next week).

I've attached the prompt set we used for the discovery evals and a short benchmark report with Redwood-verified performance profiles. Alex (cc) will add technical details and the perf profiles (TPS, latency percentiles, token costs) in his follow-up.

Next steps: can you confirm a good time next Wed/Thu for a 30m sandbox planning call? Also please confirm whether Elena should own the sandbox access on your side or if you'd like it provisioned centrally.

Thanks,
—Marissa

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the questions — below is a concise side-by-side and links to the Redwood-verified perf profiles. I've attached the prompt set we discussed with annotations and the short benchmark PDF.

Recommended model variants (based on your summarization + intent extraction workload):
- redwood-7b-instruct (float16) — high-quality, good instruction-following for extraction; recommend for initial eval.
  - Measured (hosted, single-region us-west): TPS (avg infer concurrency) ~ 3.2 reqs/s for 1-2k token requests; p50 latency ~ 180ms; p95 ~ 420ms; p99 ~ 680ms.
  - Cost estimate: ~$0.60 per 1k prompt+completion tokens (hosted).
- redwood-3b-qa (quantized int8) — lower cost, faster at shorter sequences; good fit for extraction-only paths.
  - Measured: TPS ~ 8 reqs/s for 512-token median payload; p50 ~ 90ms; p95 ~ 260ms; p99 ~ 420ms.
  - Cost estimate: ~$0.22 per 1k tokens (hosted, quantized).
- fallback: redwood-7b-instruct-quant (7b quantized) — used as an autoscale fallback when Dedicated capacity constrained, preserves quality within ~2-3% on ROUGE/F1 for extraction tasks in our evals.

Notes on measurements and what to expect:
- The latency numbers above are Redwood-verified performance profiles measured under continuous batching and realistic concurrency. The attached benchmark PDF includes the percentile curves, sequence-length distribution assumptions, and how we measured TPS.
- Dedicated pools will generally reduce variance (p99) by ~10-15% and increase sustained TPS depending on GPU config; we can model that for your expected traffic if you share target concurrency.
- For PII handling / retention: we can provision a Private/DEDICATED deployment with KMS integration. Marissa and I can walk through the security checklist on the sandbox call.

Links:
- Redwood benchmark folder (prompt sets + reports): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-finvia-benchmarks
- HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
- Public perf profile (redwood-7b-instruct): https://redwood.inference/profiles/redwood-7b-instruct

Attachments (zip of quick assets):
- finvia_prompt_set_v1.csv (annotated prompts + expected outputs)
- redwood_benchmark_report_20260316.pdf (summary of measurements & percentile charts)

If helpful, we can run a quick 1-hour sandbox where we replay ~1000 requests from your sample set and capture ROUGE/F1 + latency distribution. Suggested Thu Mar 19 09:30 PT. Let me know if that works and whether Elena or an engineer should be the attendee for the sandbox run.




—Alex
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
